page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance from the n4 family. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel x86_64 processor with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 32 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying Intel processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512, AVX_VNNI) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) for accelerated vector and matrix math. Cryptographic operations are aided by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions.

Performance benchmarks place the n4-standard-8 in the average tier for most compute tasks. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1770.0 and a multi-core score of 6838.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 530.44 GB/sec, though uncached large block writes drop to 37.65 GB/sec. The instance exhibits some performance tradeoffs, scoring in the weak category for Passmark memory and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. LLM inference on a medium 7B model is poor, yielding only 6.31 tokens/sec for text generation, though it handles smaller 135M models adequately.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density suitable for mainstream workloads that do not require specialized accelerators or high-speed local NVMe storage. Given its balanced CPU-to-memory ratio and average benchmark profile, this instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and lightweight text or image processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-8 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel processor with 4 physical cores. The architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. It does not include bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmarks indicate average performance across most compute workloads, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6838.0 and static web serving throughput of 12.95 GB/sec. However, it exhibits weaker performance in memory-bound tasks, as shown by its Passmark memory score of 1809.35, and struggles with larger LLM text generation. This instance provides a balanced, cost-effective profile for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate data processing.
